skill.name: wp-migrate
skill.description: Plan, run, and troubleshoot WordPress migrations with wp-migrate.sh, including push mode, archive imports, backups, rollback, and development workflows.
skill.summary: Plan safer WordPress migrations with wp-migrate.sh guidance for backups, dry runs, rollback, and troubleshooting.
skill.author: BWBama85

security_audit.summary: The skill is a legitimate WordPress migration guide, and most static findings are documentation false positives. Confirmed risks involve privileged setup commands, Git hook installation, temporary backup extraction, remote executable downloads, and non-interactive destructive migration mode.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before sudo commands and provide non-sudo or container alternatives where possible.
Make hook setup optional and explain that repository hooks can execute local code during commits.
Use mktemp directories with restrictive permissions and remove extracted backup data after troubleshooting.
Require dry-run review and backup confirmation before using --yes on production or shared systems.
Recommend checksum or signature verification for downloaded WP-CLI binaries before execution.

content.value_statement: WordPress migrations can risk data loss, broken URLs, and downtime. This skill guides safe wp-migrate.sh planning, dry runs, backups, rollback, and troubleshooting.
actual_capabilities: Guides push-mode WordPress migrations between SSH-accessible servers.
Explains archive imports for Duplicator, Jetpack Backup, and Solid Backups files.
Supports dry-run planning, backup review, URL alignment, and rollback preparation.
Troubleshoots SSH, WP-CLI, archive detection, disk space, and table prefix issues.
Guides source changes, builds, tests, ShellCheck, changelog updates, and pull requests.
limitations: It does not replace verified off-server backups before production changes.
It requires appropriate SSH, WP-CLI, rsync, archive, and database access.
It cannot guarantee that third-party backup archives are complete or clean.
Destructive commands and sudo setup steps still need explicit user approval.

use_cases.title: Move a WordPress Site
use_cases.description: Plan a dry run, confirm backups, migrate files and database, then verify URLs and rollback options.

use_cases.title: Automate Release Migrations
use_cases.description: Prepare CI or cron workflows with quiet mode, explicit confirmation controls, logging, and recovery steps.

use_cases.title: Recover Failed Imports
use_cases.description: Diagnose archive format, WP-CLI, disk space, table prefix, and maintenance mode problems after failed migrations.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a First Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a safe wp-migrate.sh dry run for a WordPress site. Ask for missing host, path, backup, and URL details.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Archive Import
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my WordPress backup import plan. Check archive type, disk space, destination URL handling, backups, and rollback steps.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot a Failed Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Help diagnose this wp-migrate.sh failure. Use the log symptoms I provide and suggest checks for SSH, WP-CLI, archive, and database issues.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Release Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide a wp-migrate.sh code change from source edit through build, ShellCheck, tests, changelog, commit review, and pull request notes.

output_examples.input: I need to migrate staging to production safely.
output_examples.output: A migration checklist covering dry run, verified backups, maintenance mode, URL review, execution approval, log capture, and rollback validation.

output_examples.input: My Duplicator archive import failed during database detection.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting path that checks archive structure, extracted database files, adapter selection, disk space, logs, and manual recovery options.

output_examples.input: I changed migration logic and need to open a pull request.
output_examples.output: A development workflow covering source files, build regeneration, ShellCheck, tests, changelog entry, commit review, and pull request summary.

best_practices: Run dry-run and verbose mode before touching production data.
Verify database and file backups before migrations, imports, and rollbacks.
Review every sudo, SSH, and destructive command before execution.
anti_patterns: Do not use --yes on production until the plan and backups are reviewed.
Do not import untrusted backup archives into a live site.
Do not edit generated wp-migrate.sh when source files need changes.

faq.question: What does this skill help migrate?
faq.answer: It helps with WordPress file and database migrations using wp-migrate.sh push mode or supported backup archives.

faq.question: Which backup formats are covered?
faq.answer: It covers Duplicator, Jetpack Backup, and Solid Backups workflows documented by the skill.

faq.question: Can it run a migration without changing anything?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides dry-run and verbose workflows so users can inspect planned operations first.

faq.question: Does it require server access?
faq.answer: Yes. Push migrations require SSH access, destination paths, WP-CLI, and related command-line tools.

faq.question: Can it help recover a failed migration?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains rollback, backup selection, maintenance mode cleanup, and archive troubleshooting steps.

faq.question: Is it safe for production sites?
faq.answer: It can support production work, but users must verify backups and approve destructive commands before execution.
